phrases.arabic: أَنَا جَائِع، أُرِيدُ أَنْ آكُلَ شَيْئًا
phrases.transliteration: anaa jaa2i3, ureedu an aakula shay2an

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: How are you today?

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.arabic: بِخَيْر، الْحَمْدُ لِلَّه. أَنَا سَعِيدَة الْيَوْم.
dialogue.transliteration: bikhayr, al7amdu lillaah. anaa sa3eeda al-yawm.
dialogue.english: Fine, thank God. I'm happy today.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: I'm glad to hear it.

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.transliteration: wa anta? maa bika? tabdoo mut3aban.
dialogue.english: And you? What's wrong with you? You look tired.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: أَنَا مُتْعَب جِدًّا. أَنَا قَلِق بِشَأْنِ الِامْتِحَان.
dialogue.transliteration: anaa mut3ab jiddan. anaa qaliq bishaa2ni al-imti7aan.
dialogue.english: I'm very tired. I'm worried about the exam.

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.arabic: لَا تَقْلَقْ. أَنَا أَيْضًا خَائِفَة مِنْ هَذَا الِامْتِحَان.
dialogue.transliteration: laa taqlaq. anaa aydan khaa2ifa min haadhaa al-imti7aan.
dialogue.english: Don't worry. I'm scared of this exam too.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: I'm a little upset too.

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.arabic: أَنَا جَائِعَة. أُرِيدُ أَنْ آكُلَ شَيْئًا.
dialogue.transliteration: anaa jaa2i3a. ureedu an aakula shay2an.
dialogue.english: I'm hungry. I want to eat something.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.transliteration: wa anaa jaa2i3. hayyaa na2kul ma3an.
dialogue.english: I'm hungry too. Let's eat together.

dialogue.speaker: Huda
dialogue.english: I'm glad you came.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.transliteration: wa anaa aydan. al-aana ash3uru bitahassun.
dialogue.english: Me too. Now I feel better.

lessons.culture: Asking مَا بِكَ؟ shows care, and a friend usually answers honestly but briefly. Feeling words change with the speaker: add ة for a woman, as in سَعِيد and سَعِيدَة.

exercises.prompt: A man asks you: 'كَيْفَ حَالُكَ الْيَوْم؟'. Say you are fine.
A friend asks: 'مَا بِكَ؟'. Say you are very tired (you are a man).
Complete: 'أَنَا _____ الْيَوْم' (I'm happy today, said by a woman.)
exercises.tip: A woman adds ة to the feeling word.

exercises.tip: يَسُرُّنِي first, then what pleased you.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: In my opinion, the old restaurant is better.

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.english: Maybe, but it's far.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Right. You're right.

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.english: And the prices there are high.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: لَا، لَيْسَ الْأَمْرُ كَذَلِك. الْأَسْعَارُ مُنَاسِبَة.
dialogue.transliteration: laa, laysa al-amru kadhaalik. al-as3aaru munaasiba.
dialogue.english: No, it's not like that. The prices are fair.

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: هَذَا غَيْرُ صَحِيح. أَنَا لَا أَتَّفِقُ مَعَكَ.
dialogue.transliteration: haadhaa ghayru sa7eeh. anaa laa attafiqu ma3aka.
dialogue.english: That's not true. I don't agree with you.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: حَسَنًا، مَا رَأْيُكِ فِي الْمَطْعَمِ الْجَدِيد؟
dialogue.english: OK, what do you think of the new restaurant?

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.english: Exactly, that's what I wanted to say.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: So you agree?

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.english: Yes, I agree.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Good, then we agree.

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.english: OK, that works.

response.arabic: رُبَّمَا، وَلَكِنْ فِي رَأْيِي هَذَا صَحِيح.
response.transliteration: rubbamaa, wa lakin fee ra2yee haadhaa sa7eeh.
response.english: Maybe, but in my opinion this is right.

lessons.culture: Disagreeing gently is valued: people soften a no with رُبَّمَا، وَلَكِنْ or فِي رَأْيِي before giving their view. أَنْتَ عَلَى حَقّ is a generous way to concede a point.

exercises.prompt: A friend says: 'الْمَطْعَمُ الْجَدِيدُ أَفْضَل'. Agree and tell him he is right.
A friend says: 'هَذَا غَيْرُ صَحِيح'. Politely begin your view with 'Maybe, but in my opinion'.
Complete: 'أَنْتَ عَلَى _____' (You're right.)
Complete: 'لَا _____ مَعَكَ' (I don't agree with you.)
exercises.tip: أَتَّفِقُ means 'I agree'; لَا makes it negative.

Translate into Fusha: 'No, it's not like that.'
Translate into Fusha: 'OK, that works.'
Which sentence means 'I agree' said by a woman?
exercises.tip: The ة marks a woman speaking.

Put these words in order: 'مَعَكَ / أَتَّفِقُ / لَا'.
exercises.tip: لَا comes first, then the verb.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: What's wrong with you? You look tired.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.transliteration: anaa mut3ab jiddan, wa ra2see yu2limunee.
dialogue.english: I'm very tired, and my head hurts.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: You should get some rest.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: I have a lot of work.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: It's better you go to the doctor.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: I don't think it's serious.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: لَنْ يَضُرَّكَ أَنْ تُجَرِّبَ. جَرِّبْ هَذَا الدَّوَاء.
dialogue.transliteration: lan yadurraka an tujarriba. jarrib haadhaa ad-dawaa2.
dialogue.english: It won't hurt you to try. Try this medicine.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: شُكْرًا. لَوْ كُنْتَ مَكَانِي، مَاذَا تَفْعَل؟
dialogue.transliteration: shukran. law kunta makaanee, maadhaa taf3al?
dialogue.english: Thanks. If you were me, what would you do?

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: لَوْ كُنْتُ مَكَانَكَ لَنِمْتُ مُبَكِّرًا. اِعْتَنِ بِنَفْسِكَ.
dialogue.transliteration: law kuntu makaanaka lanimtu mubakkiran. i3tani binafsika.
dialogue.english: If I were you, I'd sleep early. Take care of yourself.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: And what about the exam? I'm worried.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: Stay calm and don't rush.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.english: OK, I'll listen to your advice.

response.english: Yes, it won't hurt you to try.

lessons.culture: Advice between friends is often softened with لِمَاذَا لَا or لَوْ كُنْتُ مَكَانَكَ instead of a flat command. Verbs change for a woman, so يَنْبَغِي أَنْ تَرْتَاحِي is for her and تَرْتَاحَ is for him.

exercises.prompt: A friend says: 'أَنَا مُتْعَب جِدًّا'. Advise him to get some rest.
A friend says: 'رَأْسِي يُؤْلِمُنِي'. Tell him to try this medicine.
Complete: 'يَنْبَغِي أَنْ _____ قَلِيلًا' (You should rest, said to a woman.)
exercises.tip: The ending ي is for a woman.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'اِعْتَنِ _____' (Take care of yourself.)
exercises.tip: نَفْس means 'self'; كَ means 'your' for a man.

Translate into Fusha: 'If I were you, I'd do this.'

phrases.arabic: الطَّعَامُ بَارِدٌ قَلِيلًا، هَلْ يُمْكِنُكَ تَسْخِينَهُ لِي؟

phrases.transliteration: laa aqsidu iz3aajaka, wa lakinna haadhaa muhimm

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.english: Excuse me, there's a small problem.

dialogue.speaker: Basem
dialogue.english: Go ahead, how can I help you?

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.arabic: آسِف عَلَى الْإِزْعَاج، وَلَكِنْ هَذَا لَيْسَ مَا طَلَبْتُهُ.
dialogue.transliteration: aasif 3alaa al-iz3aaj, wa lakin haadhaa laysa maa talabtuhu.
dialogue.english: Sorry to bother you, but this isn't what I ordered.

dialogue.speaker: Basem
dialogue.english: Sorry, I'll change it for you right away.

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.arabic: وَالطَّعَامُ بَارِدٌ قَلِيلًا، هَلْ يُمْكِنُكَ تَسْخِينَهُ لِي؟
dialogue.transliteration: wat-ta3aamu baaridun qaleelan, hal yumkinuka taskheenahu lee?
dialogue.english: And the food is a bit cold, can you heat it up for me?

dialogue.speaker: Basem
dialogue.english: Certainly.

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.english: The order was very late too.

dialogue.speaker: Basem
dialogue.english: We apologise for the delay.

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.arabic: لَا أَقْصِدُ إِزْعَاجَكَ، وَلَكِنَّ هَذَا مُهِمّ. هُنَاكَ خَطَأ فِي الْفَاتُورَة.
dialogue.transliteration: laa aqsidu iz3aajaka, wa lakinna haadhaa muhimm. hunaaka khata2un fee al-faatoora.
dialogue.english: I don't mean to bother you, but this is important. There's a mistake in the bill.

dialogue.speaker: Basem
dialogue.english: I'll go over it with you.

dialogue.speaker: Adam
dialogue.arabic: هَلْ يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تُعِيدَ لِي الْمَال؟
dialogue.transliteration: hal yumkinuka an tu3eeda lee al-maal?
dialogue.english: Can you refund my money?

dialogue.speaker: Basem
dialogue.english: Certainly, forgive us.

lessons.culture: Complaints stay polite when you begin with عَفْوًا or آسِف عَلَى الْإِزْعَاج and name the problem without blame. Staff usually answer with an apology such as اِعْذُرْنَا and fix it on the spot.

challenge.title: Give an opinion and raise a problem
challenge.instructions: Write a conversation in Fusha in which a friend says how they feel, you give an opinion and disagree or agree politely, you give one piece of advice, and then you politely raise a small problem with a waiter.
required_elements: a polite complaint to a waiter

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.english: How are you today?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: أَنَا مُتْعَب قَلِيلًا، وَأَنَا قَلِق بِشَأْنِ الِامْتِحَان.
dialogue.transliteration: anaa mut3ab qaleelan, wa anaa qaliq bishaa2ni al-imti7aan.
dialogue.english: I'm a little tired, and I'm worried about the exam.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: يَنْبَغِي أَنْ تَرْتَاحَ قَلِيلًا. لَنْ يَضُرَّكَ ذَلِك.
dialogue.transliteration: yanbaghee an tartaa7a qaleelan. lan yadurraka dhaalik.
dialogue.english: You should get some rest. It won't hurt you.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: In my opinion, studying is more important.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.transliteration: rubbamaa, wa lakinna ar-raa7ata tusaa3idu aydan.
dialogue.english: Maybe, but rest helps too.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: أَنْتِ عَلَى حَقّ. حَسَنًا، هَذَا مُنَاسِب.
dialogue.english: You're right. OK, that works.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: هَيَّا نَشْرَبِ الْقَهْوَة. يَسُرُّنِي أَنَّكَ جِئْتَ.
dialogue.transliteration: hayyaa nashrabi al-qahwa. yasurrunee annaka ji2ta.

dialogue.speaker: Omar

dialogue.english: Excuse me, there's a small problem. This isn't what I ordered.

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.english: Forgive us, we'll change it right away.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
